title: Mexico City, Uruguay and Rio
summary: Lee compares Mexico City and Uruguay musicians and says recordings are leveling quality everywhere.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Oh, in Mexico City, the musicians were very good. They were very good -- especially like, I was talking about then, but since I've been in the record business, I went to Mexico to record, and you don't find any difference. Especially the way music is today, everybody is listening to records, and the tapes are shipped and that, and you get good musicians a chance to hear what someone else is playing someplace else, and they're gonna get with it. They're gonna get with it.
But the thing with traveling with -- when we went all over South America, I think the best thing about it was the

experience and the knowledge you find out about the musicians, you know, we went to Uruguay also, you know? Well, you're not gonna find too many good musicians in Uruguay, you know, because it's kind of a quaint country; it's really a beautiful little place, but I don't compare it to like, if you're gonna say Buenos Aires and if you're gonna say Caracas, and Rio and Sao Paulo St. Paul -- we went to St. Paul, also -- but it's an expereince. I believe everyone should go to Rio before they die.
